functions.name: LaunchUrlInDefaultBrowser
functions.comment:
LaunchUrlInDefaultBrowser - Opens a URL in the system's default web browser

FUNCTION CLASSIFICATION: Worker Function

ALGORITHM:
1. Call FUN_6fa12ce0 to initialize/get URL string
2. Query callback at DAT_6fa20a1c+0xb0 to get URL pointer
3. If URL is null, return 1 (failure)
4. Zero-initialize 0x7FE byte buffer for registry key path
5. Get desktop window and set foreground
6. Format registry key path: HKCR\%s\.html using FUN_6fa12b5e
7. Open registry key HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT with KEY_READ access
8. Query default value to get file type association
9. Close registry key
10. Format shell command path: HKCR\%s\%s\shell\open\command
11. Zero-initialize command buffer  
12. Open shell\open\command registry key
13. Query command line template from registry
14. Close registry key
15. Append " %1" to command (length calculation with strlen loops)
16. Append URL to command line
17. Initialize STARTUPINFO structure (0x44 bytes)
18. Call CreateProcessA with NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS (0x20)
19. On success: close process/thread handles, return 1
20. On failure: show error UI with ValidateStringId(0x14dc)
21. Dispatch inventory item handlers for cleanup
22. Reset g_nNumSubChildren to 0
23. Create UI button via CreateObjectByTypeFactory
24. Create additional UI elements (text box, etc.)
25. Set callback to FUN_6fa06a10
26. Call cleanup callback at DAT_6fa20a1c+0x78
27. Return 1

PARAMETERS: None (void)

RETURNS:
  uint - Always returns 1

GLOBALS ACCESSED:
  DAT_6fa20a1c - vtable/callback table pointer
  DAT_6fa218f8 - initialization byte
  g_nNumSubChildren - count of child UI elements
  g_apSubChildrenArray - array of child element pointers
  g_dwCurrentInputItem - current input focus item
  g_dwInventorySubState - inventory UI state
  g_UITypeInventoryButton - button factory type
  g_UITypeInventoryTextBox - text box factory type
  _g_pfnSubPanelCallback - sub-panel callback function pointer

REGISTRY KEYS:
  HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\.html - gets default file type
  HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\<filetype>\shell\open\command - gets browser command

SPECIAL CASES:
  - Function boundaries appear broken in Ghidra (single instruction body)
  - Decompiler infers parameters from stack usage patterns
  - Falls back to error UI if registry query or process launch fails
  - Creates up to 32 (0x1F + 1) child UI elements with assert check

ERROR HANDLING:
  - Registry open/query failures fall through to error UI path
  - CreateProcessA failure triggers ValidateStringId error display
  - FogAssert called if g_nNumSubChildren >= 32

functions.name: InvokeCallbackOnArrayElements
functions.signature: void InvokeCallbackOnArrayElements(void * pArrayBase, dword dwElementStride, int nElementCount, void * pfnCallback)
functions.comment:
Iterates over array elements and invokes callback function on each.

Classification: Worker function - array callback iterator

Algorithm:
1. Decrement element count and check if negative (skip if count <= 0)
2. Save registers (EBX, EBP, ESI, EDI)
3. Load callback pointer into EBX
4. Load stride into EBP
5. Load array base into ESI (current element pointer)
6. Set loop counter EDI = count
7. Loop: Set ECX = current element pointer, CALL callback
8. Advance pointer: ESI += stride
9. Decrement counter, repeat until zero
10. Restore registers and return

Parameters:
  pArrayBase (void *) - Base address of array to iterate
  dwElementStride (dword) - Byte offset between elements (e.g., 2 for Unicode chars)
  nElementCount (int) - Number of elements to process
  pfnCallback (void *) - Function pointer called with ECX = element address

Returns: void

Calling Convention: __stdcall (callee cleans 0x10 bytes)

Usage Context:
Called by FUN_6fa07aa0 to initialize Unicode arrays:
  InvokeCallbackOnArrayElements(local_c0, 2, 0x10, _default_constructor_closure)
This calls default constructor on 16 Unicode elements with 2-byte stride.

Register Usage in Callback:
  ECX = pointer to current array element (passed as this pointer)
  Callback is responsible for initializing/processing that element

14. Call vtable[0x44] to get password data pointer

16. Run message pump with MessagePumpPasswordCallback

18. If password not cancelled and MCP connected (Ordinal_10002) and not in error (Ordinal_10046 == 0):

functions.name: EditBoxKeyHandler

functions.comment:
EditBoxKeyHandler - Callback for handling special key presses in Battle.net chat edit box

Classification: Callback/Handler - Invoked by edit control for special key events

Algorithm:
1. Check if key code is 0x0E (autocomplete trigger from chat history)
2. If key is TAB (0x09):
   a. Check if autocomplete entries exist (g_dwAutocompleteEntryCount != 0)
   b. Increment current autocomplete index
   c. Wrap index to 0 if exceeds entry count
   d. Convert selected autocomplete entry to Unicode and set in edit box
   e. Return 0 (handled)
3. If key is not TAB and not 0x0E, return 1 (not handled)
4. For 0x0E key (history insertion):
   a. Get current edit box text via D2Win_GetEditBoxChild
   b. If no text or no chat history buffer, return 0
   c. Convert edit box Unicode text to ANSI (acStack_600)
   d. Get history text from buffer (acStack_500)
   e. Calculate combined length of current text + history text
   f. If combined length exceeds 255 chars, return 0 (overflow protection)
   g. Split current text at cursor position into prefix and suffix
   h. Build new string: prefix + history + suffix using sprintf
   i. Convert result to Unicode and update edit box
5. Return 0

Parameters:
  nUnused (uint) - Unused first parameter (stack-based calling convention padding)
  nCursorPosition (size_t) - Current cursor position in edit box text
  lpszKeyCode (char *) - Pointer to key code byte triggering callback

Returns:
  0 - Key was handled (TAB autocomplete or history insertion)
  1 - Key was not handled (pass to default handler)

Special Cases:
  - TAB cycles through autocomplete entries with wraparound
  - History insertion protects against buffer overflow (255 char limit)
  - Empty edit box or missing history buffer causes early return
  - Cursor position used to split text for inline history insertion

2. Call sub-initialization functions (FUN_6fa10090, FUN_6fa0f490)
3. Dispatch inventory item handlers for inventory slots 1-8 to clear them
4. Set current input item and pointer from global state
5. Loop through existing sub-children array, dispatching handlers to clear each
6. Reset g_nNumSubChildren to 0, clear g_dwInventorySubState
7. Call FUN_6fa117b0 for additional state reset
8. Clear g_dwInventoryExtraState, dispatch handlers for slots 9-10
9. If g_dwSpecialModeFlag == 1, call FUN_6fa127f0 (special mode handler)
10. If g_dwInventoryPanelMode == 3, reset panel mode to 0
11. If g_pInventoryPanelState is valid, set bit mask via SetOrClearBitMask
12. Create 7 child UI objects via CreateObjectByTypeFactory, each with bounds check
    - Each creation validates g_nNumSubChildren < 32 (0x1f), asserts on overflow
    - Child object types: g_ChildObjectType1 through g_ChildObjectType7
    - Objects stored in g_apSubChildrenArray at current index
13. After creating second child object, call ValidateStringId(0x14c5) and add text
14. Set final created object as current input item
15. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
  None - Function takes no parameters

Returns:
  int - Always returns 1 indicating successful initialization

Local Variables:
  pnCreatedObject (int *): Pointer to newly created UI child object from factory
  nLoopIndex (int): Loop counter for iterating sub-children array
  pdwSlotPtr (uint *): Pointer to current slot in inventory type array during iteration

Special Cases:
- Asserts with FogAssert if sub-children count exceeds 31 (max 32 children)
- Calls FUN_6fa12bdd(0xffffffff) on overflow which does not return

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1f (31): Maximum sub-children index (array size 32)
- 0x1086: Source line number for assertion
- 0x14c5: String ID for text box content
- Panel mode 3: Special mode requiring reset to 0

- g_dwInventorySubState: Set to 0
- g_dwInventoryExtraState: Set to 0
- g_dwInventoryPanelMode: May be set to 0 if was 3
- g_apSubChildrenArray: Populated with 7 new child objects

functions.name: UpdateCharacterClassListScrollPosition
functions.comment:
Periodically scans text box lines for character class prefixes and updates scroll position.

Classification: Timer/Callback - called periodically to sync UI display with character list

Algorithm:
1. Get current tick count and compare against g_dwPanelDisplayTimeout
2. If timeout not elapsed or g_dwInventoryExtraState is null, exit early
3. Get starting line number from GetTextBlockField58(g_dwInventoryExtraState)
4. Calculate max scan range as min(startLine + 16, g_szCommandBufferEnd)
5. For each line in range [startLine, maxLine):
   a. Get line text via TextBoxGetLineChar
   b. Convert Unicode to ANSI via Unicode::unicode2Win into local buffer
   c. Compare against g_szCharacterClassPattern ("-" prefix for class abbrevs)
   d. If match found (strcmp==0):
      - Calculate page index: ((lineNum + rounding) >> 4) << 4
      - Store to g_dwPanelStateA and jump to update
6. After loop, if g_fClassListEnabled != 0, proceed to update
7. If g_dwLastScrollPosition != g_dwPanelStateA:
   a. Copy g_byPanelDisplayFlags to g_byPanelDisplayMode
   b. Store g_dwPanelStateA to g_dwPanelStateB
   c. Call Ordinal_10027 (D2Win scroll/display update)
   d. Set next timeout to GetTickCount() + 1000ms
   e. Update g_dwLastScrollPosition

Parameters:
  nUnused (Stack+4) - int - Unused parameter (stdcall cleanup)

Returns:
  int - Always returns 1

Local Variables (Hungarian naming - function body incomplete in Ghidra):
  DVar2 -> dwTickCount: DWORD from GetTickCount
  nLineNum: int loop counter (already named)
  iVar5 -> nStrCmpResult: int strcmp return value
  iVar6 -> nMaxLineIndex: int max line to scan
  pUVar3 -> pUnicodeLine: Unicode* line text pointer
  pbVar4 -> pbLocalBuffer: byte* pointer into abStack_100
  pbVar7 -> pbPattern: byte* pointer into g_szCharacterClassPattern
  bVar1 -> byCurrentChar: byte current char being compared
  bVar8 -> fCharLess: bool comparison flag
  abStack_100 -> abAnsiBuffer: byte[256] ANSI conversion buffer

Special Cases:
- Early exit if tick count < g_dwPanelDisplayTimeout (rate limiting)
- Early exit if g_dwInventoryExtraState is null
- Character class pattern: "-\0\0\0asn\0dru\0bar\0pal\0nec\0sor\0ama"
- Page calculation rounds line number to nearest 16

Globals Modified:
- g_dwPanelStateA: Target scroll position (page-aligned line number)
- g_dwPanelStateB: Active scroll position being displayed
- g_byPanelDisplayMode: Display mode byte
- g_dwPanelDisplayTimeout: Next allowed update tick
- g_dwLastScrollPosition: Cached last scroll position for change detection

NOTE: Function body incomplete in Ghidra - only entry instruction visible.
Decompiler produces correct output via flow analysis but variables cannot
be renamed via MCP tools. Run RecreateFunction_6fa06fe0.java script to fix.

functions.name: InitializePanelDisplayText
functions.signature: void InitializePanelDisplayText(char * lpszDisplayText, int nTextMode, int nPanelType)
functions.comment:
Initializes panel display text and sets display mode flags based on text mode and panel type.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_dwInventoryExtraState is non-zero (panel system active)
2. If inactive, return immediately (early exit)
3. Copy display text string to global buffer g_szPanelDisplayText
4. Calculate display flags based on nTextMode and nPanelType:
   - nPanelType=0, nTextMode=0: flags = 0x09
   - nPanelType=0, nTextMode!=0: flags = 0x00
   - nPanelType!=0, nTextMode=0: flags = 0x1b (27)
   - nPanelType!=0, nTextMode!=0: flags = 0x23 (35)
5. Store flags to g_byPanelDisplayFlags and g_byPanelDisplayMode
6. Reset panel state values (g_dwPanelStateA, g_dwPanelStateB = -1)
7. Call Ordinal_10059 with nPanelType parameter
8. Set display timeout to GetTickCount() + 1000ms

Parameters:
  lpszDisplayText (ECX) - char* - Text string to display on panel
  nTextMode (EDX) - int - Text display mode (0=standard, non-zero=alternate)
  nPanelType (Stack+4) - int - Panel type (0=simple panel, non-zero=extended panel)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Returns immediately if g_dwInventoryExtraState == 0 (panel system inactive)
  - Flag calculation uses NEG/SBB/AND pattern for branchless conditional assignment

Caller Context:
  - Called from FUN_6fa118b0 after selecting panel display functions based on DAT_6fa3e9f0/DAT_6fa3e9f4 flags

functions.name: UpdatePanelDisplayState
functions.comment:
Updates panel display state by synchronizing display flags and decrementing state counter.

Classification: Worker function - updates UI panel state variables

Algorithm:
1. Copy g_byPanelDisplayMode to first byte of g_byPanelDisplayFlags (sync current mode)
2. Calculate new state: g_dwPanelStateA = g_dwPanelStateA - g_dwPanelStateDecrement
3. Clamp result to zero if negative (using branchless: result & ((result < 1) - 1))
4. Store clamped value back to g_dwPanelStateA
5. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
  nUnused (int) - Unused parameter, passed for callback compatibility (stdcall convention)

Returns:
  int - Always returns 1 (TRUE/success)

Globals Accessed:
  g_byPanelDisplayMode (0x6fa1b05c) - READ - Current panel display mode (byte)
  g_byPanelDisplayFlags (0x6fa1b054) - WRITE - Panel display flags, first byte updated
  g_dwPanelStateA (0x6fa1b058) - READ/WRITE - Panel state counter (uint)
  g_dwPanelStateDecrement (0x6fa208e0) - READ - Decrement amount for state counter (uint)

Special Cases:
  - If g_dwPanelStateA <= g_dwPanelStateDecrement, result is clamped to 0 (prevents underflow)

Calling Convention: __stdcall (cleans 4 bytes from stack via RET 4)

functions.name: ResetInventoryPanelState
functions.comment:
Resets the inventory panel state by clearing all inventory slots and sub-children.

Classification: Cleanup function - Called during panel transitions/close operations.

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6fa10090 to perform initial cleanup (dispatches handlers for 30 inventory data items)
2. Call FUN_6fa0f490 to perform secondary cleanup (dispatches handlers for 11 inventory data items)
3. Dispatch inventory item handlers for 8 fixed inventory slots (g_dwInventorySlot1-8)
4. Set current input item from g_dwCurrentInputItem
5. Set current input pointer from g_pCurrentInputPointer
6. Loop through g_apSubChildrenArray dispatching handlers for each sub-child (0 to g_nNumSubChildren-1)
7. Reset g_nNumSubChildren to 0
8. Reset current input item from g_dwCurrentInputItem
9. Reset g_dwInventorySubState to 0
10. Call FUN_6fa117b0 for additional cleanup
11. Reset g_dwInventoryExtraState to 0
12. Dispatch handlers for inventory slots 9 and 10
13. If g_dwSpecialModeFlag == 1, call FUN_6fa127f0
14. If g_dwInventoryPanelMode == 3, reset it to 0
15. If g_pInventoryPanelState != NULL, call SetOrClearBitMask with bit 1

Parameters: None (void)

Returns: bool - Always returns TRUE (1) indicating success

Globals Modified:
- g_nNumSubChildren: Reset to 0
- g_dwInventorySubState: Reset to 0
- g_dwInventoryExtraState: Reset to 0
- g_dwInventoryPanelMode: Reset to 0 if was 3

Memory Model:
- No allocations performed
- Modifies global state variables only
- Uses g_pInventoryPanelState pointer if non-NULL

functions.name: ResetInventoryPanelToInitialState
functions.comment:
Resets the inventory panel UI to its initial state, clearing all slots and handlers.

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6fa10090 and FUN_6fa0f490 for panel pre-reset cleanup
2. Dispatch inventory item handlers for slots 1-8 (addresses 0x6fa21818-0x6fa21838)
3. Set current input item and pointer from global state
4. Loop through sub-children array (g_apSubChildrenArray), dispatching handlers for each
5. Reset g_nNumSubChildren to 0, call SetCurrentInputItem again
6. Clear g_dwInventorySubState to 0
7. Call FUN_6fa117b0 for additional state reset
8. Clear g_dwInventoryExtraState, dispatch handlers for slots 9-10
9. If g_dwSpecialModeFlag == 1, call FUN_6fa127f0
10. If g_dwInventoryPanelMode == 3, reset it to 0
11. If g_pInventoryPanelState is non-null, set bit mask with value 1
12. Clear 9 panel state slots (g_dwPanelResetFlag through g_dwPanelStateSlot8)
13. Set g_szCommandBufferEnd to 1000 (0x3E8)
14. Check game list data byte at offset 0x225 and Ordinal_10002 result
15. If conditions met: show string 0x1413, reset panel, clear buttons, create text box, return 1
16. Otherwise: assert max children (0x20), create objects via factory, setup UI elements
17. Return 1 on success

Parameters:
  None (uses global state)

Returns:
  int - Always returns 1 (success)

SSA Temporaries (compiler-generated, cannot be renamed):
  piVar1: int * - pointer to created object from CreateObjectByTypeFactory
  iVar2: int - loop counter for sub-children iteration, also holds Ordinal_10002 result

Special Cases:
- If sub-children count exceeds 0x1F (31), triggers FogAssert with file/line info
- Special mode flag (0x6fa3e9cc) triggers additional processing via FUN_6fa127f0
- Panel mode 3 is special case that gets reset to 0

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1413: String ID for special mode text
- 0x14C6: String ID for normal mode text
- 0x1086: Assert line number for max children check
- 0x20 (32): Maximum allowed sub-children count
- 0x3E8 (1000): Command buffer end value
- 0xFFFFFFFE (-2): Panel scroll offset reset value
- 0x23: Panel display mode value
- 0x10: Panel state decrement value

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10002: Checks special condition (returns 0 for special path)
- Ordinal_10012: Called during normal panel setup to finalize display

functions.name: PopulateLadderPanelEntries
functions.signature: void PopulateLadderPanelEntries(uint dwStartIndex, int nEntryCount, int nEntryStride, byte byDisplayFlags, int * pLadderEntryData)
functions.comment:
Populates ladder panel entries with player ranking data or displays "not on ladder" message.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if g_dwInventoryExtraState is null
2. If nEntryCount == 0 (reset mode):
   a. Initialize Unicode buffers (aUStack_200/400/600/700) for message formatting
   b. Get player name via FUN_6fa11910
   c. Format "Player %s is not on the ladder" message
   d. Reset panel state: dispatch handlers for slots 1-10, clear sub-children
   e. Reset inventory state flags and callback pointer
   f. Handle special mode (g_dwSpecialModeFlag == 1) and panel mode 3
   g. Clear button frames and create text box with formatted message
3. If byDisplayFlags matches g_byPanelDisplayFlags (populate mode):
   a. Navigate scrollbar to dwStartIndex if g_dwPanelStateA == -1
   b. Initialize character class name array (ama/sor/nec/pal/bar/dru/ass)
   c. Calculate end index (min of dwStartIndex+nEntryCount, g_szCommandBufferEnd)
   d. For each entry from dwStartIndex to end index:
      - Extract entry flags from pLadderEntryData[2]
      - Compare entry name against g_szPanelDisplayText (highlight current player)
      - Set line color (0 for match, 4 or 5 based on flags)
      - Format rank number via FUN_6fa13454 to column 0
      - Get character title via CalculateCharacterTitleTier (class, difficulty, expansion flags)
      - Concatenate title + player name to column 1
      - Set character class name to column 2 (from class name array)
      - Format level to column 3
      - Format experience as abbreviated number to column 4
      - Advance entry pointer by nEntryStride + 0xC

Parameters:
  dwStartIndex (ECX): Starting row index in ladder panel
  nEntryCount (EDX): Number of entries to populate (0 = reset mode)
  nEntryStride (Stack+0x4): Byte stride between ladder entries beyond fixed 12-byte header
  byDisplayFlags (Stack+0x8): Display flags that must match g_byPanelDisplayFlags
  pLadderEntryData (Stack+0xC): Pointer to ladder entry array

Returns:
  void

Ladder Entry Structure (inferred at pLadderEntryData offset):
  +0x00: Experience low dword
  +0x04: Experience high dword  
  +0x08: Flags dword (bits 0-3=class, 4=?, 5=expansion, 6=hardcore, 8-12=difficulty, 16-23=level)
  +0x0C: Player name (null-terminated string)

Character Class Mapping (bits 0-3):
  0=Amazon, 1=Sorceress, 2=Necromancer, 3=Paladin, 4=Barbarian, 5=Druid, 6=Assassin

Flag Bits in Entry Flags:
  0x0F: Class mask (0-6)
  0x10: Unknown flag (affects color)
  0x20: Expansion character flag
  0x40: Hardcore character flag
  0x1F00: Difficulty mask (bits 8-12)

Text Columns:
  0: Rank number
  1: Title + Player name
  2: Character class abbreviation
  3: Character level
  4: Experience (abbreviated)

functions.name: InitializeCharacterClassSelectionPanel
functions.comment:
Initializes the character class selection panel UI for Diablo II.

Creates and configures button controls for each character class (Amazon, Sorceress,
Necromancer, Paladin, Barbarian, and conditionally Druid/Assassin for expansion).
Also sets up game mode indicator text boxes (Hardcore, Expansion, Ladder, Classic).

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 7 Unicode string buffers for class abbreviations
2. Convert ANSI class codes (AMA, SOR, NEC, PAL, BAR, DRU, ASN) to Unicode
3. Create class selection buttons (descriptors 0x6B-0x72):
   - Slot 1 (0x6B): First class button, frame value 1 (selected)
   - Slots 2-6 (0x6C-0x70): Class buttons, frame value 0 (unselected)
   - Slots 7-8 (0x71-0x72): Druid/Assassin (expansion only)
4. Create corresponding text labels (descriptors 0x73-0x7A)
5. Add sub-child objects for game mode labels with bounds checking (max 32)
6. Create character info text field (descriptor 0x69) with column formatting
7. Configure stat display columns via Ordinal_10059 calls
8. Call FUN_6fa09350 for additional panel setup
9. Create selection timer (descriptor 0x7D) and set handler
10. Clear panel display text global

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
- Druid/Assassin buttons only created if g_dwPanelResetFlag != 0 (expansion mode)
- Asserts if g_nNumSubChildren >= 32 (0x20) before adding child objects

Magic Numbers:
- 0x6B-0x72: Character class button descriptor indices
- 0x73-0x7A: Character class label descriptor indices
- 0x67: Character info label descriptor
- 0x69: Character stats text field descriptor
- 0x7D: Selection timer descriptor
- 0x14CE: String ID for first class label
- 0x14C8-0x14CC: String IDs for game mode labels (Hardcore/Expansion/Ladder/Classic)
- 0xFD9: String ID for character info label
- 0x10: Unicode buffer size (16 wide chars)
- 0x1086: Assert line number for max children check

Ordinal Functions:
- Ordinal_10056: D2Win.SetTextColor - Sets text rendering color
- Ordinal_10059: D2Win.AddStatValue - Adds stat value to display column

functions.name: InitializePanelDisplayDefault
functions.comment:
Initializes panel display to default state, resetting slots and creating UI elements.

Algorithm:
1. Clear 9 panel state slots (g_dwPanelResetFlag through g_dwPanelStateSlot8) to 0
2. Clear g_dwInventoryExtraState to 0
3. Set g_szCommandBufferEnd to 1000 (0x3E8)
4. Check if game list data byte at offset 0x225 is non-zero
5. If set, call Ordinal_10002 to check special game mode condition
6. If Ordinal_10002 returns 0 (special path):
   a. Validate string ID 0x1413
   b. Call FUN_6fa10090 and FUN_6fa0f490 for pre-reset cleanup
   c. Dispatch inventory item handlers for slots 1-8
   d. Set current input item and pointer from global state
   e. Loop through sub-children array dispatching handlers
   f. Reset g_nNumSubChildren to 0, call SetCurrentInputItem again
   g. Clear g_dwInventorySubState to 0, call FUN_6fa117b0
   h. Clear g_dwInventoryExtraState, dispatch slots 9-10

   j. If g_dwInventoryPanelMode == 3, reset to 0

   b. Create first object via factory (g_TextBoxObjectType1), add to sub-children
   c. Increment g_nNumSubChildren, re-check limit
   d. Create second object via factory (g_TextBoxObjectType2), add to sub-children
   e. Validate string ID 0x14C5, add text to created object
   f. Call FUN_6fa07aa0 for additional setup

   h. Set g_byPanelDisplayMode to 0x23
   i. Set g_dwPanelStateDecrement to 0x10
   j. Set _g_dwPanelTimerValue to 1000
   k. Call Ordinal_10012 to finalize panel setup

Parameters:
  None (uses global state)

Returns:
  void

SSA Temporaries (compiler-generated, cannot be renamed):
  iVar1: int - Ordinal_10002 result, also loop counter for sub-children
  piVar2: int * - pointer to created object from CreateObjectByTypeFactory
  pdwInventoryType: uint * - pointer iterating through sub-children array
  wszText, wszText_00: wchar_t * - text strings from ValidateStringId

- Special mode flag at 0x6fa3e9cc == 1 triggers FUN_6fa127f0
- Panel mode 3 is special case that gets reset to 0

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1413: String ID for special mode text
- 0x14C5: String ID for normal mode text
- 0x1086: Assert line number for max children check
- 0x20 (32): Maximum allowed sub-children count
- 0x3E8 (1000): Command buffer end value / timer value
- 0xFFFFFFFE (-2): Panel scroll offset reset value

functions.name: InitializeOrResetInventoryPanel
functions.comment:
Initializes or resets inventory panel state based on game context.

Algorithm:
1. Reset panel state flags (g_dwPanelResetFlag and slots 1-8) to 0
2. Reset g_dwInventoryExtraState to 0, set g_szCommandBufferEnd to 1000
3. Check game list data flag at offset 0x225
4. If flag set, call Ordinal_10002 (D2Lang.GetLocaleId)
5. If Ordinal_10002 returns 0 (cleanup path):
   a. Validate string ID 0x1413 for panel text
   b. Call panel initialization helpers FUN_6fa10090 and FUN_6fa0f490
   c. Dispatch inventory handlers for slots 1-8
   d. Restore current input item and pointer
   e. Loop through sub-children array, dispatching handlers for each
   f. Reset g_nNumSubChildren to 0, restore input item again
   g. Clear g_dwInventorySubState, call FUN_6fa117b0
   h. Clear g_dwInventoryExtraState, dispatch slots 9-10
   i. If special mode flag is 1, call FUN_6fa127f0
   j. If panel mode is 3, reset to 0
   k. If panel state pointer valid, toggle bit masks (set then clear)
   l. Reset all button frames to 0

6. Else (initialization path):
   a. Assert sub-children count < 32 (0x20)
   b. Create text box from g_TextBoxObjectType1, add to sub-children
   c. Increment sub-children count, assert < 32 again
   d. Create text box from g_TextBoxObjectType2, add to sub-children

   g. Set scroll offset to -2, display mode to 0x23

   i. Call Ordinal_10012 (D2Lang.GetCurrentLanguageId)

Parameters: None (reads global state)

Returns: void

- Two distinct paths: cleanup (Ordinal_10002 returns 0) vs initialization

Magic Numbers:
- 0x225: Offset into game list data for active flag
- 0x1413: String ID for cleanup path text
- 0x14c6: String ID for initialization path text
- 0x20 (32): Maximum sub-children count
- 0x1086 (4230): Assert line number

- 0x10 (16): Panel state decrement value
- 1000: Timer/command buffer value

functions.name: InitializeOrResetCharSelPanel
functions.comment:
Initializes or resets the character selection panel based on game state.

This function operates in two modes:
- RESET MODE: When in an active game session (game list flag set, Ordinal_10002 returns 0)
  cleans up existing panel state, resets all inventory slots, and clears sub-children
- INIT MODE: Otherwise, creates new text box objects for character selection UI and
  initializes the character class selection panel

Algorithm:
1. Set panel reset flag to 1 (active reset)
2. Clear all 8 panel state slots (g_dwPanelStateSlot1-8) to 0
3. Clear inventory extra state and set command buffer end to 1000
4. Check if game list data at offset 0x225 is non-zero (active session flag)
5. If active session, call Ordinal_10002 (D2Multi.IsMultiplayerGame check)
6. If Ordinal_10002 returns 0 (RESET MODE):
   a. Validate string ID 0x1413 and call FUN_6fa10090, FUN_6fa0f490
   b. Dispatch inventory handlers for slots 1-8
   c. Set current input item and pointer from globals
   d. Loop through sub-children array, dispatching handlers for each
   e. Reset sub-children count to 0
   f. Clear inventory sub-state and call FUN_6fa117b0
   g. Clear extra state and dispatch slots 9-10
   h. If special mode flag == 1, call FUN_6fa127f0
   i. If panel mode == 3, reset to 0
   j. Toggle bit mask on panel state (set then clear)
   k. Reset all 4 button frame values to 0
   l. Create text box and add text, clear callback
7. Else (INIT MODE):
   a. Assert sub-children count < 32
   b. Create first text box from g_TextBoxObjectType1, add to sub-children
   c. Increment count, assert still < 32
   d. Create second text box from g_TextBoxObjectType2, add to sub-children
   e. Increment count
   f. Validate string ID 0x276A, add text to second text box
   g. Initialize character class selection panel

functions.name: AddMotdMessageAndUpdateDisplay
functions.signature: void AddMotdMessageAndUpdateDisplay(void * this, int nMessageId, char * lpszMessageText)
functions.comment:
Adds or updates a Message of the Day (MOTD) entry in the sorted linked list and refreshes the display.

Algorithm:
1. Search g_pMotdMessageList for existing node with matching nMessageId
2. If found, skip to step 6 to update text
3. If not found, allocate new 0x208-byte node via FogMemAlloc
4. Store nMessageId at node+0x200
5. Insert node into sorted position (ascending by nMessageId):
   - If list empty or nMessageId < first node's ID, prepend to list
   - Otherwise, traverse to find correct sorted position and insert
6. Copy lpszMessageText to node buffer (max 0x200 bytes) with null terminator
7. Initialize 512-element Unicode array on stack
8. If g_pInventoryPanelState is NULL, return early
9. Concatenate all MOTD messages from linked list into szConcatBuffer (max 0x200 bytes):
   - Traverse linked list appending each message
   - Calculate strlen via manual loop after each append
   - Stop if total length exceeds 0x1ff
10. Set visibility of g_pMotdTextBox (hide if has content, show if empty)
11. Convert concatenated ANSI string to Unicode via win2Unicode
12. Display Unicode text in g_pInventoryPanelState text box

Parameters:
  this (ECX) - IMPLICIT: Message ID (int cast as void* due to __thiscall)
  nMessageId - Message ID for sorting (unused due to ECX mapping)
  lpszMessageText - ANSI message text to store (max 512 chars)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if g_pInventoryPanelState is NULL (no UI to update)
  - Existing entries are updated in place, not duplicated
  - Messages are sorted by ID in ascending order
  - Total concatenated length capped at 0x200 bytes

Structure Layout (MOTD Node - 0x208 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field       Type      Description
  0x000   0x200 szMessage   char[512] ANSI message text
  0x200   0x4   nMessageId  int       Message sort key
  0x204   0x4   pNext       char*     Next node pointer

Magic Numbers:
  0x208 - MOTD node allocation size (512 + 4 + 4)
  0x200 - Message buffer size and Unicode array count
  0x1780 - Source file line number for FogMemAlloc debug

functions.name: SkipChannelNamePrefix
functions.comment:
Extracts channel name by skipping the asterisk prefix marker.

CLASSIFICATION: Leaf utility - string parsing helper

Algorithm:
1. Search for asterisk (*) character (0x2A) in input string using strchr
2. If asterisk not found, return original string unchanged
3. If asterisk found but next character is null terminator, return original string
4. Otherwise return pointer to character immediately after asterisk

Parameters:
  lpszChannelName (ECX) - Input string potentially prefixed with "*ChannelName"

Returns:
  char* - Pointer to character after asterisk if valid prefix found
          Original string pointer if no asterisk or asterisk at end

SPECIAL CASES:
  - NULL result from strchr returns original string
  - Asterisk at string end (e.g., "name*") returns original string
  - Multiple asterisks only skips first one

USAGE CONTEXT:
  Battle.net channel names use asterisk prefix for channel type indicators.
  This function strips the prefix to get the actual channel/user name.
  Called by ProcessChatCommandAndUIMessage to extract whisper targets.
  Called by profile panel functions to parse channel member names.

MAGIC NUMBERS:
  0x2A - ASCII asterisk '*' character

functions.name: ExtractPrefixBeforeWildcard
functions.comment:
ExtractPrefixBeforeWildcard - Extract substring from source up to first '*' wildcard character

Classification: Worker function - String manipulation utility for wildcard prefix extraction

Algorithm:
1. Check if source string starts with '*' character
2. If source starts with '*', jump to full string copy (no prefix extraction needed)
3. Search for '*' character in source string using strchr
4. If '*' not found, copy entire source to destination using SStrCopy
5. If '*' found, calculate prefix length (pointer difference)
6. Copy prefix bytes using optimized DWORD copy (4 bytes at a time via MOVSD.REP)
7. Copy remaining bytes individually (0-3 bytes via MOVSB.REP)
8. Null-terminate destination string at prefix length position

Parameters:
  lpszSource (char *) [ECX] - Source ANSI string potentially containing wildcard '*'
  lpszDestination (char *) [EDX] - Destination buffer for extracted prefix substring

Returns:
  void - Destination buffer contains extracted prefix or full copy of source

Special Cases:
  - Source starting with '*': Full string copy (no prefix exists)
  - No '*' in source: Full string copy
  - Empty source: Copies empty string
  - Memory copy optimization: Uses REP MOVSD/MOVSB for efficient byte copying

Caller Context:
  EditBoxKeyHandler (0x6fa04a50) - Called to extract history text prefix before wildcard
  for chat autocomplete insertion, splitting history entry from suffix pattern

functions.name: ProcessBnetAdvertisementData
functions.comment:
Processes Battle.net advertisement data received via callback.

Classification: Callback/Handler - invoked through vtable dispatch.

Algorithm:
1. Call callback vtable method at offset 0x24 to retrieve ad message data into stack frame
2. If callback returns 0 (no data), return 0 immediately
3. Switch on nMessageType:
   - Case 0: Process string handler - calculate string length via REPNE SCASB,
             dispatch to handler function from g_apfnBnetAdHandlers[dwParam] if dwParam < 0x18
   - Case 2: Copy string - copy 16 bytes from dwParam buffer to g_szBnetAdCopyBuffer
   - Case 3: Play video advertisement:
     a. Cleanup existing UI object via CleanupUnitType9
     b. Get temp path via GetTempPathA, fallback to "." if fails
     c. Create temp filename with "BNetAd" prefix via GetTempFileNameA
     d. Delete previous temp file at g_szBnetAdTempPath
     e. Create new temp file for write (CREATE_ALWAYS, FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE)
     f. Write video data (pvStack_318, DStack_314 bytes) to temp file
     g. Close file handle
     h. Extract file extension from pcStack_320 via strrchr('.')
     i. Call FUN_6fa1350c with extension character
     j. Initialize Smacker video player with temp file path
     k. Copy temp path to g_szBnetAdTempPath for later cleanup
     l. Store dwParam in g_dwBnetAdParam
     m. Release two pool allocations
4. Return 1 on success

Parameters: (IMPLICIT - populated by callback)
  nMessageType [ESP+0x0]: Message type selector (0=string handler, 2=copy, 3=video)
  dwParam [ESP+0x8]: Parameter value or buffer pointer depending on message type
  pcStack_320 [ESP+0x10]: Pointer to source filename with extension
  DStack_314 [ESP+0x1C]: Size of video data in bytes
  pvStack_318 [ESP+0x18]: Pointer to video data buffer

Returns:
  0 - Callback returned no data
  1 - Message processed successfully

Special Cases:
  - Message type 0 with dwParam >= 0x18: Silently ignored, returns 1
  - Message type 0 with NULL handler: Silently ignored, returns 1
  - GetTempPathA failure: Falls back to "." (current directory)
  - CreateFileWrapper failure (returns -1): Skips write but continues processing

Magic Numbers:
  0x24 - Callback vtable offset for GetAdData method
  0x18 - Maximum handler index in g_apfnBnetAdHandlers table (24 handlers)
  0x10 - Copy buffer size for message type 2
  0x104 - MAX_PATH (260 bytes) for temp path buffers
  0x40000000 - GENERIC_WRITE for CreateFile
  0x4 - CREATE_ALWAYS disposition
  0x8000000 - FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE
  0x2e - ASCII '.' for extension search
  0x36a, 0x36b - Pool allocation IDs for ReleasePoolAllocation

functions.name: AdjustBnetListScrollPosition
functions.comment:
Adjusts the Battle.net list scroll position by a delta and updates scroll arrow UI states.

Classification: Worker function - Core scroll position management for Battle.net list UI

Algorithm:
1. Save current scroll position in dwPreviousScrollPosition for change detection
2. Initialize scroll arrow flags (nCanScrollUp, nCanScrollDown) to 0 (disabled)
3. Check if content is scrollable (lineCount >= 12 visible lines):
   - If fewer than 12 lines: Reset scroll position to 0, skip to step 8
   - Calculate dwMaxScrollPosition = lineCount - 11 (visible window size)
4. Calculate new position = currentPosition + nScrollDelta
5. Clamp position to valid range [0, dwMaxScrollPosition]:
   - If newPosition < 0: Clamp to 0 via bitwise AND trick
   - If newPosition > dwMaxScrollPosition: Clamp to max
6. Set nCanScrollUp = 1 if scrollPosition > 0 (can scroll toward top)
7. Set nCanScrollDown = 1 if scrollPosition < dwMaxScrollPosition (can scroll toward bottom)
8. If position changed: Call FUN_6fa0b4d0 to re-render list items
9. Update scroll arrow UI objects via SetUnitBitMask:
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[0xB]: Up arrow primary (uses nCanScrollUp)
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[0xC]: Down arrow primary (uses nCanScrollDown)
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[0xD]: Up arrow secondary (uses nCanScrollUp)
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[0xE]: Down arrow secondary (uses nCanScrollDown)

Parameters:
  nScrollDelta (int, ECX): Scroll amount - positive scrolls down, negative scrolls up
                          Common values: 1/-1 (single line), 10/-10 (page), -1 (scroll to top)

Returns:
  void

Globals Accessed:
  g_dwAutomapScrollPosition (0x6fa21aa0): Current scroll position (READ/WRITE)
  g_dwAutomapLineCount (0x6fa21a9c): Total line count in list (READ)
  g_apBnetUIObjects[0xB-0xE]: Scroll arrow UI objects (READ for pointer)

Callees:
  FUN_6fa0b4d0: Re-renders visible list items after scroll position change
  SetUnitBitMask: Updates UI object visibility/state flags

Callers:
  ScrollAutomapUp (0x6fa01f10): Passes delta=10 for page-up scroll
  ScrollBnetListUp (0x6fa01f30): Passes delta=-1 for scroll-to-top

Magic Numbers:
  0xB (11): Visible lines in scroll window
  0xC (12): Minimum lines needed for scrolling to be enabled
  0xB-0xE: UI object indices for scroll arrows (up/down pairs)

Clamping Logic (bitwise trick at 0x6fa0a977-0x6fa0a97f):
  Uses SETLE/DEC/AND to clamp negative values to 0:
  - SETLE CL: Sets CL=1 if newPos <= 0, else CL=0
  - DEC ECX: CL=1 becomes 0, CL=0 becomes -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)
  - AND EAX,ECX: If newPos was negative, mask is 0, result is 0

functions.name: HandleGameSlotButtonClick
functions.comment:
Handles click events on game slot buttons in the Battle.net multiplayer game list UI.

Algorithm:
1. Search g_apGameSlotButtons array to find which button triggered the event
2. Calculate absolute slot index = scroll position + button array index
3. If button not found in array, return 0 (event not handled)
4. Branch based on event type (pEventData[1]):
   - 0x205 (WM_RBUTTONUP): Show user profile panel
   - Other: Select game slot

RIGHT-CLICK PATH (0x205 - Show Profile):
5. Traverse game list linked list to find node at slot index
6. Call FUN_6fa117b0 to clean up any existing profile panel
7. Extract username from node+0x4, find '*' separator (strchr)
8. Compare extracted name with current user's name (g_pGameListData+0x88)
9. If names differ: Call FUN_6fa11510 to show OTHER user's profile (read-only)
10. If names match: Call FUN_6fa111c0 to show OWN profile (editable)

LEFT-CLICK PATH (Select Slot):
11. Get current tick count for double-click detection
12. If clicking already-selected slot (g_nSelectedSlotIndex == index):
    - Deselect current slot, clear selection bit mask
    - Reset g_pChatHistoryBuffer and g_nSelectedSlotIndex to null/-1
    - Update UI button states based on input field and selection
13. If clicking new slot (index < g_dwAutomapLineCount):
    - Deselect previous selection if any
    - Traverse list to target node
    - Set selection bit mask on target node
    - Update g_pChatHistoryBuffer, g_nSelectedSlotIndex, g_dwSlotSelectionTickCount
    - Update all UI button visibility states

Parameters:
  pEventData (dword *) - Event structure pointer:
    +0x00: Button handle (dword) - matches g_apGameSlotButtons entry
    +0x04: Event type (dword) - 0x205 = WM_RBUTTONUP (right-click)

Returns:
  1 - Event handled successfully
  0 - Event not handled (button not found in array)

Game List Node Structure (stride 0xa0 = 160 bytes):
  +0x04: char[] Username (may contain '*' separator for display name)
  +0x36: char[] Profile description field
  +0x88: char[] Current user's display name (in g_pGameListData)
  +0x8a: ushort Flags - bit 2 (0x04) and bit 5 (0x20) control profile display
  +0x9c: uint * Unit handle pointer (must not be NULL)
  +0xa0: Node * pNext - linked list next pointer

UI Object Indices (g_apBnetUIObjects):
  [0]: Send button - enabled when input has text
  [1]: Reply button - enabled when chat history selected and input has text  
  [3]: Squelch button - enabled when selection has no squelch flag
  [4]: Unsquelch button - enabled when selection has squelch flag
  [5]: Unknown button - mirrors [0] state

Globals Modified:
  g_pChatHistoryBuffer - Points to selected game list node (or 0)
  g_nSelectedSlotIndex - Current slot index (or -1 if none)
  g_dwSlotSelectionTickCount - Tick count when slot was selected

Magic Numbers:
  0x205 - WM_RBUTTONUP message (right mouse button up)
  0x2a - ASCII '*' character for strchr search
  0xa0 - Game list node stride (160 bytes)
  0x88 - Offset to username in g_pGameListData
  0x9c - Offset to unit handle pointer in node
  0x8a - Offset to flags word in node

Error Handling:
  Asserts if unit handle (node+0x9c) is NULL when accessing selection

functions.name: SubmitChatEditBoxInput
functions.comment:
Submits the current chat edit box input for processing.

CLASSIFICATION: Callback/Handler - UI callback invoked when user submits chat input

ALGORITHM:
1. Get Unicode text from current input edit box via D2Win_GetEditBoxChild
2. If edit box child is NULL, return success (1)
3. Get length of Unicode text via Unicode::strlen
4. If text is empty (length 0), return success (1)
5. Convert Unicode text to ANSI (Windows code page) via Unicode::unicode2Win

   - Max conversion size: 0x100 (256) characters
6. Call ProcessChatCommandAndUIMessage with converted ANSI text and nWhisperMode=0
7. Return result from ProcessChatCommandAndUIMessage

PARAMETERS:
  None (parameterless callback)

RETURNS:
  int - Always 1 on empty/null input; otherwise result from ProcessChatCommandAndUIMessage

SPECIAL CASES:
  - Empty input text silently returns 1 (success)
  - NULL edit box child returns 1 (success)
  - Conversion uses fixed 256-byte buffer (max input length limitation)

GLOBALS ACCESSED:
  g_pCurrentInputPointer (0x6fa218d0) - Current input edit box control pointer

CROSS-REFERENCES:
  - Referenced from function pointer table at 0x6fa1b170
  - Called by UI system as submit callback for chat input

STACK FRAME:
  [ESP+0x4] to [ESP+0x103] - acAnsiBuffer[256]: ANSI conversion buffer

functions.comment:
Submits current chat input with whisper mode enabled.

functions.name: HandleSquelchPlayerButtonClick
functions.comment:
Handles the squelch player button click in Battle.net chat UI.

Algorithm:
1. Early return if no chat history buffer is selected
2. Copy player name from chat buffer offset +4 (strlen + memcpy pattern)
3. Throttle squelch commands to once per 1000ms via GetTickCount()
4. Store current tick as last squelch timestamp
5. Search for asterisk in player name (for character wildcard)
6. Format squelch command string "/squelch *%s" with player name
7. If chat buffer has valid unit pointer at offset 0x9c:
   a. Assert unit pointer is non-null (FogAssert on failure)
   b. Get unit ID and apply bit mask from gdwInvBitMasks_exref+0x28
   c. Write masked value back to unit
   d. Clear g_pChatHistoryBuffer and reset g_nSelectedSlotIndex to -1
8. Get edit box text via D2Win_GetEditBoxChild
9. Set fHasText flag based on edit box content
10. Update UI button visibility for indices 5, 0 based on fHasText
11. Update UI button visibility for index 1 based on buffer and text state
12. Check unit ID bit mask from gdwBitMasks_exref+0x24 for squelch state
13. Update UI button visibility for indices 3, 4 based on squelch state
14. Call callback vtable function at offset 0x74
15. If callback returns non-zero: call vtable+0x14, clear edit box, return 1
16. Otherwise: validate string ID 0x14e7 and show sub-panel UI

Parameters:
  (none) - This is a __stdcall callback with no parameters

Returns:
  uint - 1 on early return or callback success, 0 when showing sub-panel

Special Cases:
- Returns 1 immediately if g_pChatHistoryBuffer is null
- Returns 1 if GetTickCount() is within 1000ms of last squelch
- Calls FUN_6fa12bdd(-1) (abort) if unit pointer assertion fails

Local Variables:
- cVar1 (chCurrent): char - Current character during strlen iteration
- DVar2 (dwCurrentTick): uint - GetTickCount result for throttling
- pUVar3 (pwszEditText): wchar_t* - Edit box Unicode text pointer
- iVar4 (nTextLength): int - Unicode string length result
- wszPanelText (pwszPanelText): wchar_t* - Sub-panel text pointer
- uVar5 (dwStrLen): uint - String length / bit mask result
- uVar6 (dwLoopCounter): uint - DWORD copy loop counter
- pcVar7 (pszSource): char* - Source string pointer for copy
- iVar8 (fHasText): int - Boolean flag for edit box content
- pcVar9 (pszDest): char* - Destination string pointer for copy
- acStack_200 (szPlayerName): char[256] - Player name buffer
- auStack_100 (abCommandBuffer): byte[256] - Formatted command buffer

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x9c: Offset to unit pointer in chat history buffer structure
- 0x28: Offset to inverse bit mask in gdwInvBitMasks_exref
- 0x24: Offset to bit mask in gdwBitMasks_exref
- 0x74: Callback vtable offset for squelch validation
- 0x14: Callback vtable offset for squelch execution
- 0x14e7: String resource ID for squelch confirmation dialog
- 1000: Throttle interval in milliseconds

Global Dependencies:
- g_pChatHistoryBuffer: Pointer to selected player's chat entry

functions.name: RenderBnetListVisibleItems
functions.comment:
Renders visible items in the Battle.net game list UI.

Algorithm:
1. If game list is empty, return immediately
2. Detach head node from global list, prepare for insertion sort
3. For each remaining node in unsorted list:
   a. Calculate priority based on state flags (bit 1=4, bit 3=3, bit 0=2, bit 2=1, else 0)
   b. Find insertion point in sorted list by comparing priorities
   c. Insert node at correct position (higher priority first)
4. Restore sorted list to global head pointer
5. Initialize Y position to 0x46 (70 pixels), item index to 0
6. For each item in sorted list:
   a. If item index outside visible range [scroll_pos, scroll_pos+11):
      - Build render flags for non-visible item (hidden state)
   b. If item index within visible range:
      - Call SetUnitField14 to set Y position on composite unit
      - Build render flags based on game properties
      - Apply alternating row highlight on odd indices
      - Advance Y position by 0x3C (60 pixels per row)
   c. Write render flags to composite unit via WriteValueToPointer
   d. Advance to next node

Parameters:
  None (void)

Returns:
  void

Structure Layout (Game List Node):
  Offset  Size  Field        Description
  0x8a    2     wFlags       Item flags (bit 2=passworded, bit 3=full, bit 5=expansion, bits 8-12=difficulty)
  0x90    4     dwState      State flags (bit 0=joinable, bit 1=private, bit 3=ladder, bit 5=hardcore)
  0x9c    4     pUnit        Pointer to CompositeUnit for UI rendering
  0xa0    4     pNext        Next node pointer in linked list

Flag Bits (wFlags at +0x8a):
  0x04 - Game is password protected
  0x08 - Game is full
  0x20 - Expansion game
  0x1F00 - Difficulty level (5 bits, shifted >> 8)

State Flags (dwState at +0x90):
  0x01 - Joinable game
  0x02 - Private game
  0x08 - Ladder game
  0x09 - Combined joinable/ladder check
  0x20 - Hardcore mode

Bitmask Offsets (gdwBitMasks/gdwInvBitMasks):
  +0x10 - Full game indicator
  +0x14 - Password protected indicator
  +0x18 - Difficulty tier low bit
  +0x1C - Difficulty tier high bit
  +0x20 - Alternating row highlight
  +0x24 - Hardcore mode indicator
  +0x28 - Selected item indicator
  +0x2C - Joinable/ladder combined
  +0x30 - Expansion mode indicator

Magic Numbers:
  0x46 (70) - Initial Y position for first visible item
  0x3C (60) - Vertical spacing between list items
  0x0B (11) - Maximum visible items in list window

Globals Referenced:
  g_pGameListHead (0x6fa21a90) - Head of game list linked list
  g_dwAutomapScrollPosition (0x6fa21aa0) - Current scroll position
  g_pChatHistoryBuffer (0x6fa21aa4) - Selected game node pointer
  gdwBitMasks_exref - External bitmask array for setting flags

functions.name: AddOrUpdateBnetGameEntry
functions.signature: byte * AddOrUpdateBnetGameEntry(byte * pbGameName, uint * pdwOptions, uint dwGameId)
functions.comment:
Adds a new game entry to the Battle.net game list or updates an existing entry.

Algorithm:
1. Search linked list g_pGameListHead for existing game entry matching pbGameName
2. For each node, compare game names (stripping leading '*' prefix)
3. If match found: update dwGameId at offset 0x90, call ParseGameNodeDescriptionString
4. Determine display type (1 or 5) based on flags at offset 0x8A
5. If existing match: call InitCompositeUnitWeapon, RenderBnetListVisibleItems, return node
6. If no match: allocate new 0xA4-byte game node structure via FogMemAlloc
7. Zero-initialize structure (0x29 DWORDs), copy game name to offset +4
8. Set dwGameId at offset 0x90, call ParseGameNodeDescriptionString
9. Create CompositeUnit for display; if creation fails, retry with default params
10. Assert ptNode->hUnit is not null (fatal error if null)
11. Set emblem icon if emblem ID at offset 0x94 is non-zero
12. Call SetUnitFieldValue with 0x23B, SetDataFieldWithValidation with 0
13. Initialize random seed with GetTickCount on first call
14. Set scaled random value on composite unit
15. Initialize Unicode buffers for display strings
16. Convert game name and description to Unicode
17. Handle game name prefix/suffix parsing (split on '*' character)
18. Check game type signature (D2DV=0x44324456, D2ST=0x44325354, D2XP=0x44325850)
19. Call SetCompositeUnitStrings with Unicode display strings
20. Append new node to end of g_pGameListHead linked list
21. Increment g_dwAutomapLineCount, format status text
22. Update scroll position bounds (max visible = 11 items)
23. Enable/disable scroll arrows via SetUnitBitMask on UI objects
24. Call RenderBnetListVisibleItems to refresh display
25. Return pointer to game node structure

Parameters:
- pbGameName (ECX): ANSI game name string, may contain '*' separator
- pdwOptions (EDX): Pointer to options flags array
- dwGameId (Stack+4): Unique game identifier

Returns:
- Pointer to game node structure (0xA4 bytes) on success
- Never returns null; asserts and terminates on failure

Game Node Structure Layout (0xA4 bytes):
Offset  Size    Field           Description
0x00    4       dwGameType      Game type signature (D2DV/D2ST/D2XP)
0x04    50      szGameName      Game name string (ANSI)
0x36    48      szDescription   Game description string
0x66    16      abComponentIds  Component ID array
0x76    16      abColorIds      Color ID array
0x86    1       bDefaultClass   Default class for fallback
0x88    2       wReserved       Reserved
0x8A    2       wFlags          Display flags (bit 2: type, bit 3: modifier)
0x90    4       dwGameId        Game identifier
0x94    1       bEmblemId       Emblem icon ID
0x95    1       bEmblemColor1   Emblem primary color
0x96    1       bEmblemColor2   Emblem secondary color
0x9C    4       hUnit           Composite unit handle
0xA0    4       pNext           Next node in linked list

Magic Numbers:
- 0xA4: Game node structure size
- 0x2A: ASCII '*' delimiter character
- 0x658: Source line number for allocation
- 0x685: Source line for assertion
- 0xB (11): Maximum visible game list items
- 0x23B: Unit field ID for list item
- 0x44324456: "D2DV" - Diablo 2 Classic
- 0x44325354: "D2ST" - Diablo 2 Stress Test
- 0x44325850: "D2XP" - Diablo 2 Expansion

functions.name: ParseGameNodeDescriptionString
functions.signature: byte ParseGameNodeDescriptionString(void * this, char * pszDescription, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
ParseGameNodeDescriptionString - Parses a game description string and populates game node fields

Algorithm:
1. Calculate string length of description using strlen loop (SCASB.REPNE pattern)
2. Clear game node flags field at offset 0x8A to zero
3. Check dwFlags bits to determine game type code:
   - Flag 0x02 set: return type 0x11 (Private game)
   - Flag 0x08 set: return type 0x12
   - Flag 0x01 set: return type 0x10
   - Flag 0x04 set: return type 0x15
   - Flag 0x1400 set: return type 0x13
   - No flags + short string: return type 0x07 (Unknown)
4. If string too short (<4 bytes), skip product code parsing
5. Read 4-byte product code from description start, copy to node offset 0x00
6. Match product code against known values:
   - 0x44545354 "TSDT": type 0x0A if extended parsing
   - 0x44325850 "D2XP": parse extended D2 format
   - 0x44324456 "D2DV": parse extended D2 format
   - 0x44325354 "D2ST": parse extended D2 format
   - 0x43484154 "CHAT": type 0x14 (Chat)
   - 0x4452544c "RLTD": type 0x0A
   - 0x44534852 "RSHR": type 0x0A
   - 0x53534852 "SSHR": type 0x0D
   - 0x4a535452 "RSTR": type 0x0D
   - 0x53455850 "SXEP": type 0x0E
   - 0x53544152 "STAR": type 0x0D
   - 0x5732424e "W2BN": type 0x0F
7. For D2 products (D2XP, D2DV, D2ST), parse comma-separated fields:
   - Field 1 to offset 0x46 (game name)
   - Field 2 to offset 0x36 (game password?)
   - DecodeVariableInt14 for value
   - Copy 11 bytes to offset 0x66 (class data), pad remaining with 0xFF
   - If class data valid, parse trailer:
     - Byte at offset 0x86 (adjusted by -1)
     - Copy 11 bytes to offset 0x76, pad with 0xFF
     - Byte to offset 0x88 (ushort)
     - DecodeVariableInt14 to offset 0x8A
     - DecodeVariableInt14 to offset 0x8C
     - Bytes to offsets 0x94, 0x95, 0x96 (convert 0xFF to 0)
8. For unknown products: set code to "NKNU", copy node name to offset 0x36
9. Final loop: initialize 16 bytes at offsets 0x66 and 0x76 with special pattern

Parameters:
  this (ECX)         - void *: Pointer to GameNode structure to populate
  pszDescription     - char *: Game description string (product code + comma-separated fields)
  dwFlags            - uint: Flags controlling parsing behavior and type selection
                       Bit 0x01: Type 0x10
                       Bit 0x02: Type 0x11 (Private game)
                       Bit 0x04: Type 0x15
                       Bit 0x08: Type 0x12
                       Bit 0x1400: Type 0x13

Returns:
  byte: Game type classification code (0x07-0x16)

Magic Numbers:
  Product Codes (4-char LE):
    0x554e4b4e = "NKNU" (Unknown product fallback)
    0x44545354 = "TSDT"
    0x44325850 = "D2XP" (Diablo II: Lord of Destruction)
    0x44324456 = "D2DV" (Diablo II)
    0x44325354 = "D2ST" (Diablo II Stress Test?)
    0x43484154 = "CHAT" (Chat channel)
    0x4452544c = "RLTD"
    0x44534852 = "RSHR"
    0x53534852 = "SSHR"
    0x4a535452 = "RSTR"
    0x53455850 = "SXEP"
    0x53544152 = "STAR" (StarCraft)
    0x5732424e = "W2BN" (Warcraft II Battle.net Edition)

GameNode Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size   Field
  0x00    4      Product code (DWORD)
  0x04    0x32   Node name string
  0x36    0x10   Parsed field 2 / fallback name
  0x46    0x10   Parsed field 1 (game name)
  0x66    0x10   Class data array (padded with 0xFF)
  0x76    0x10   Secondary data array (padded with 0xFF)
  0x86    1      Class byte (adjusted -1 from input)
  0x88    2      Trailer byte 1 (ushort)
  0x8A    2      Flags (short from DecodeVariableInt14)
  0x8C    2      Value (short from DecodeVariableInt14)
  0x94    1      Color/attribute byte 1
  0x95    1      Color/attribute byte 2
  0x96    1      Color/attribute byte 3

functions.name: ProcessBnetPlayerJoinNotification
functions.signature: int ProcessBnetPlayerJoinNotification(void * this, byte * pbGameData, uint * pdwOptions)
functions.comment:
Processes a Battle.net player join event and displays a notification in the chat channel.

Algorithm:
1. Call AddOrUpdateBnetGameEntry to register/update the player in the game list
2. Check if player notifications are enabled (g_fPlayerNotificationsEnabled)
3. If disabled, skip notification and return success
4. Calculate player name string length using SCASB.REPNE at offset +0x36 in entry
5. Format join message using szFmtPlayerJoinedChannel ("%s has joined the channel.")
6. Initialize Unicode buffer (576 wchar_t elements) with default constructor
7. Convert ANSI message to Unicode using win2Unicode
8. Validate Unicode string length is under 500 characters (assert if exceeded)
9. Get filter string from string ID 0xF9A using ValidateStringId
10. Find and remove all occurrences of filter string from message
11. Display filtered message in chat text box with color code 5

Parameters:
  this (ECX, IMPLICIT): Game ID passed to AddOrUpdateBnetGameEntry as dwGameId
  pbGameData: Pointer to player data structure containing name at offset +0x36
  pdwOptions: Options passed to AddOrUpdateBnetGameEntry

Returns:
  int: Always returns 1 (success)

Special Cases:
  - If notifications disabled, returns immediately after updating game entry
  - If Unicode string exceeds 499 characters, triggers FogAssert and calls FUN_6fa12bdd(-1)
  - Filter string removal loop continues until no matches or end of filtered match

Magic Numbers:
  0x36 - Offset to player name within game entry structure
  0x240 - Unicode buffer size (576 elements)
  0x1F4 - Max string length validation (500)
  0xF9A - String ID for filter pattern
  5 - Chat text color code for join messages

functions.name: ResetBnetGameListAndButtonStates
functions.comment:
Resets the Battle.net game list UI state and updates button visibility.

Algorithm:
1. If chat history buffer exists with selected unit at offset 0x9c:
   a. Assert unit pointer is non-null (line 0x7d1)
   b. Get unit ID and clear selection flag via WriteValueToPointer
   c. Clear g_pChatHistoryBuffer and set g_nSelectedSlotIndex to -1
2. Get edit box text from g_pCurrentInputPointer
3. Set fHasText flag if edit box has non-empty text (Unicode::strlen > 0)
4. Update UI button states based on fHasText:
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[5] and [0] - enabled if text exists
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[1] - enabled if text AND selection exist
5. Check selection unit flags via GetUnitIdFromPointer:
   - Extract flag at gdwBitMasks_exref+0x24 (bit 9, 0x200)
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[3] - enabled if selection exists but flag clear
   - g_apBnetUIObjects[4] - enabled if selection AND flag set
6. Release all game list entries:
   - Iterate g_pGameListHead linked list (next at +0xa0)
   - Release composite unit at +0x9c, clear pointer
   - Free each node via ReleasePoolAllocation
   - Set g_pGameListHead to 0
7. Release all channel list entries:
   - Iterate g_pChannelListHead linked list (next at +0x44)
   - Free each node via ReleasePoolAllocation
   - Set g_pChannelListHead and g_pChannelListTail to 0
8. Reset g_dwAutomapLineCount to 0
9. Format empty game count text with szFmtGameCount
10. Initialize Unicode buffer (576 elements, 0x240)
11. Convert ANSI buffer to Unicode via win2Unicode
12. Update game list display via SetGameListText
13. Calculate scroll position based on line count:
    - If lineCount <= 11: scroll position = 0
    - If lineCount > 11: max scroll = lineCount - 11
    - Set fCanScrollUp and fCanScrollDown flags
14. If scroll position non-zero, call RenderBnetListVisibleItems
15. Update scroll button states:
    - g_apBnetUIObjects[0xb,0xd] - up arrows enabled by fCanScrollUp
    - g_apBnetUIObjects[0xc,0xe] - down arrows enabled by fCanScrollDown

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Asserts if g_pChatHistoryBuffer exists but unit pointer at +0x9c is null
  - Scroll buttons only enabled when game list exceeds 11 visible items (12+)

Structure Layout (Game List Node):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type        Description
  0x9c    4     pCompositeUnit  void *      Composite unit handle
  0xa0    4     pNextEntry      void *      Next node in linked list

Structure Layout (Channel List Node):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type        Description
  0x44    4     pNextEntry      void *      Next node in linked list

UI Object Indices:
  0     - Send button (enabled with text)
  1     - Action button (enabled with text AND selection)
  3     - Whisper button (enabled with selection, no friend flag)
  4     - Friend button (enabled with selection AND friend flag)
  5     - Text indicator (enabled with text)
  0xb   - Scroll up button (game list)
  0xc   - Scroll down button (game list)
  0xd   - Scroll up button (channel list)
  0xe   - Scroll down button (channel list)

Magic Numbers:
  0x7d1  - Assert line number (2001)
  0x9c   - Offset to unit pointer in game list entry
  0xa0   - Offset to next pointer in game list entry
  0x44   - Offset to next pointer in channel list entry
  0x28   - Offset in gdwInvBitMasks_exref for clear mask
  0x24   - Offset in gdwBitMasks_exref for friend flag (bit 9)
  0x240  - Unicode buffer element count (576)
  0xb    - Visible game list item count threshold (11)
  0xc    - Line count threshold for scroll (12)

functions.name: RemovePlayerFromChannelList
functions.comment:
Removes a player from the Battle.net channel player list.

Searches the linked list starting at g_pGameListHead for a player matching
the given name. When found, displays a notification message if enabled,
unlinks the node from the list, and releases associated resources.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize pPrevNode = NULL, pCurrentNode = g_pGameListHead
2. Loop through linked list comparing player name at offset +0x04
3. If match found (strcmp returns 0):
   a. If notifications enabled (g_fPlayerNotificationsEnabled != 0):
      - Format "[name] has left the channel" message
      - Convert to Unicode and display in chat text box
   b. Unlink node: if pPrevNode == NULL, update head; else update prev->next
   c. If removed node was selected in chat history:
      - Clear selection (g_pChatHistoryBuffer = 0, g_nSelectedSlotIndex = -1)
      - Call UpdateUIElementsOnTextChange()
   d. Release composite unit at node offset +0x9C
   e. Call ReleasePoolAllocation()
4. Decrement g_dwAutomapLineCount (player count)
5. Update game list text with new count
6. Adjust scroll position:
   a. If count < 12, reset scroll to 0
   b. Otherwise clamp scroll to valid range [0, count - 11]
7. Update scroll arrow UI elements based on scroll position
8. Call RenderBnetListVisibleItems() to refresh display
9. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
  lpszPlayerName - Pointer to null-terminated player name string to remove

Returns:
  1 - Always returns success

Structure Layout (Player Node at iVar9):
  Offset | Size | Field              | Type    | Description
  -------+------+--------------------+---------+---------------------------
  +0x00  | 4    | dwNodeType         | uint    | Node type or flags
  +0x04  | 50   | szPlayerName       | char[]  | Player name string
  +0x36  | ?    | szDisplayName      | char *  | Display name pointer
  +0x9C  | 4    | pCompositeUnit     | void *  | Associated unit pointer
  +0xA0  | 4    | pNextNode          | Node *  | Next node in linked list

Magic Numbers:
  0x0C (12) - Visible row count threshold for scroll handling
  0x0B (11) - Visible rows minus one (count - 11 = max scroll)
  0x05      - Text color/style for chat notification
  0x240 (576) - Unicode buffer size in characters

Globals Used:
  g_pGameListHead           - Head of player linked list
  g_fPlayerNotificationsEnabled - Enable/disable leave notifications
  g_pChatHistoryBuffer      - Currently selected chat entry
  g_nSelectedSlotIndex      - Selected slot index (-1 = none)
  g_dwAutomapLineCount      - Total player count in list
  g_dwAutomapScrollPosition - Current scroll position
  g_apBnetUIObjects[]       - Array of UI element pointers (indices 0xB-0xE)

functions.name: RemovePatternFromUnicodeString
functions.comment:
Removes all occurrences of a pattern substring from a Unicode string in-place.

Algorithm:
1. Get length of input string, assert < 500 chars
2. Get pattern string from string ID 0xf9a via ValidateStringId
3. Get pattern length
4. Search for pattern in string using Unicode::strstr
5. Loop while pattern found AND character after match is not null terminator:
   a. Get remaining string length from match position
   b. Calculate bytes to move: (remainingLen - patternLen) * 2
   c. Shift remaining characters left using Unicode_memmove
   d. Search for next pattern occurrence
6. Return (void)

Parameters:
  pUszString (ECX): Unicode string to modify in-place

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Asserts if string length >= 500 (calls FogAssert then FUN_6fa12bdd(-1))
  - Pattern at end of string (followed by null) terminates loop
  - Empty result possible if string contains only pattern

Called By:
  - FUN_6fa0c580: Channel player leave notification formatting
  - Other BNet message formatting functions (3 callers total)

functions.name: OnBnetChannelJoined
functions.comment:
Battle.net channel join callback - handles the event when user joins a channel.

Algorithm:
1. Format "You have joined channel: %s" message with channel name
2. Initialize Unicode buffer array (576 elements, 1152 bytes)
3. Convert ANSI message to Unicode
4. Validate Unicode string length < 500, assert if exceeded
5. Get string ID 0xF9A via ValidateStringId (returns pattern to strip)
6. Strip all occurrences of pattern from message (removes special markers)
7. Add formatted message to chat text box with style 5 (system message)
8. Copy channel name to g_pGameListHead global buffer (inline strcpy)
9. Copy channel name to g_pGameListData+0x359 (game list channel field)
10. If g_pGameListData+0x379 is empty, copy channel name there too
11. Loop through g_apGameSlotButtons array, set bit 1 on each button
12. Clear bit mask on g_pScrollListControl
13. Call ResetBnetGameListAndButtonStates to reset game list UI

functions.name: FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty
functions.comment:
Fetches game list from callback vtable and filters by player difficulty level.
Called during multiplayer game list refresh to populate the visible game list
with games matching the player's current difficulty setting.

Algorithm:
1. Call callback vtable function at offset 0x38 to get raw game list data
2. Return early if no data returned (NULL pointer)
3. Extract game count from first dword and store in g_nGameListCount
4. Initialize filtered entry counter (nFilteredCount) to 0
5. For each game entry in the raw list:
   a. Set entry flag word to 1 at (pnDestEntry - 2)
   b. Copy game ID from source[3] to pnDestEntry[0]
   c. Calculate string length using REPNE SCASB (strlen equivalent)
   d. Copy game name string to (pnDestEntry - 0x36) using MOVSD.REP/MOVSB.REP
   e. If g_pTextControl not NULL, convert game name to Unicode
   f. Assert game name pointer is valid, exit on failure
   g. Skip past game name string (find null terminator)
   h. Skip past second string (description), find difficulty byte
   i. Extract difficulty level byte after second string
   j. Calculate max difficulty threshold: ((flags & 0x1f00) / 0x500) + 1
   k. Apply difficulty filter:
      - If expansion bit (0x04) NOT set: filter if (difficulty - '0') > threshold
      - If expansion bit set: filter if (difficulty - '3') > threshold, or if difficulty <= '2'
   l. If game passes filter: copy description, increment nFilteredCount, advance pnDestEntry by 0x3b
   m. If game filtered out: decrement g_nGameListCount
   n. Skip past remaining string to next entry
6. Call FUN_6fa0edb0 to finalize the filtered game list display

Parameters: None (uses global state)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- NULL game list data from callback: exits immediately after cleanup call
- NULL string pointers during parsing: triggers FogAssert and exits with code -1
- Difficulty filtering differs between expansion (bit 4 set) and classic modes
- Classic mode: difficulty characters '0'-'9' where '0' is Normal
- Expansion mode: difficulty characters '3'-'9' where '3' is Normal

Structure Layout (Game Entry - 0x3b bytes stride):
Offset  Size  Field           Description
-0x38   2     wEntryFlag      Entry validity flag (set to 1)
-0x36   50    szGameName      Null-terminated game name string
0x00    4     dwGameId        Game ID from source data
+0x11   ?     szDescription   Game description string (copied from source)

Magic Numbers:
0x38 - Offset to GetGameList function in callback vtable
0x3b - Stride between game list entries (59 bytes)
0x1ea - Offset to difficulty flags in g_pGameListData
0x1f00 - Mask for difficulty level bits (bits 8-12)
0x500 - Division factor for difficulty level calculation
0x04 - Expansion mode flag bit
0x30 - ASCII '0' for classic difficulty base
0x33 - ASCII '3' for expansion difficulty base
0x32 - ASCII '2' for filtering expansion games in classic mode

7. Copy game name string (from input+0x1c) via strlen + memcpy to entry+0x01
8. Copy description string (from input+0x2c) via strlen + memcpy to entry+0x11
9. Increment global game list count

Parameters:

    +0x08: wGameId (short) - Game type/ID for duplicate detection
    +0x14: wFlags (short) - Game flags
    +0x1c: szGameName (char[16]) - Null-terminated game name
    +0x2c: szDescription (char[16]) - Null-terminated description

Returns:

Special Cases:
  - Early return if game ID already exists in list
  - String copy uses optimized DWORD copy then byte copy for remainder

  Offset  Size  Field              Type    Description
  0x00    1     padding            byte    Unused padding
  0x01    16    szGameName         char[]  Game name string

  0x31    2     wFlags             short   Game flags from input+0x14
  0x33    2     wGameId            short   Game ID from input+0x08

functions.comment:

functions.name: InitiateGameListRequest
functions.comment:
InitiateGameListRequest - Initiates a game list request for multiplayer game browsing

Classification: Worker function - prepares request parameters and dispatches to D2MCPCLIENT

Algorithm:
1. Set inventory panel mode to 3 (game list view)
2. Reset game list count to 0
3. Check difficulty mode byte at g_pGameListData+0x356
4. If difficulty != 0x02 (Nightmare): delegate to FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty and return
5. For Hell difficulty (0x02): zero 24-byte request buffer (6 DWORDs via REP STOSD)
6. Check expansion flag bit 0x04 at g_pGameListData+0x1EA
7. If expansion flag set: OR dwRequestFlags with 0x800 (expansion filter flag)
8. Increment g_wSessionRequestId until non-zero (handles wraparound)
9. Call D2MCPCLIENT.Ordinal_10006 to send game list request
10. Save current session ID to g_wLastSessionRequestId for response matching

Parameters: None (void function)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Non-Hell difficulty: Delegates to FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty
- Session ID wraparound: Loop ensures ID is never 0 after increment

- g_dwInventoryPanelMode: Set to 3 (game list panel)
- g_nGameListCount: Reset to 0
- g_wSessionRequestId: Incremented (non-zero guaranteed)
- g_wLastSessionRequestId: Updated to match sent request

- 0x04: Expansion mode flag (triggers 0x800 in request flags)

- 0x800: Expansion-only games filter

functions.name: FinalizeFilteredGameListDisplay
functions.comment:
Refreshes the game list UI control with filtered game entries and restores selection.

    - Entry names start at g_aGameListEntriesDest + 1 (offset into entry)

  void

functions.name: OnGameListSelectionClick

   b. Convert Unicode to ANSI in local buffer
   c. Increment session request ID (avoiding zero)

   a. Get game description from g_aszGameListDescriptions array
   b. Calculate string length (inline strlen)

functions.name: PopulateGameListDetails
functions.comment:
Populates the game list secondary control with detailed game information.

Displays game name, elapsed time, level restrictions, max players, and
character roster with class names for a selected multiplayer game entry.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pGameListSecondaryControl exists, return if null
2. Clear existing text data from the control
3. Check game name at offset +0x2C for non-empty string
4. If game name exists, add game name and newline to control
5. Calculate elapsed time from seconds at offset +0x0C:
   - Hours = seconds / 3600
   - Minutes = (seconds % 3600) / 60
   - Seconds = seconds % 60
6. Format and display "Elapsed Time: H:MM:SS"
7. Check level restriction byte at offset +0x11 (max level diff)
   - If 0: Display single level from offset +0x10
   - If 1-99: Display level range "Level X to Y"
   - If >= 100: Skip level display
8. Check max players byte at offset +0x12
   - If 1-7: Display "Up to N Players"
9. Add newline separator
10. Loop through player roster (count at offset +0x14):
    - Character names at offset +0x8C (16-byte stride)
    - Character class at offset +0x4C (2-byte stride)
    - Character level at offset +0x6C (2-byte stride)
    - Format class-specific string based on class ID (0-6)
    - Display using StringAsciiToUnicode with style 5
11. Reset scrollbar to top position

Parameters:
  pGameInfo (ECX) - Pointer to GameListEntry structure containing:
    +0x0C: dwElapsedSeconds - Elapsed time in seconds
    +0x10: byMinLevel - Minimum character level
    +0x11: byMaxLevelDiff - Maximum level difference (0=single, 1-99=range)
    +0x12: byMaxPlayers - Maximum players (1-7)
    +0x14: dwPlayerCount - Player count in game
    +0x2C: szGameName[32] - Game name string
    +0x4C: awCharClass[8] - Character class IDs (0-6)
    +0x6C: awCharLevel[8] - Character levels
    +0x8C: aszCharName[8][16] - Character names (16 bytes each)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
  - Empty game name (length 0): Skips game name display
  - Level diff >= 100: Skips level restriction display
  - Max players 0 or >= 8: Skips player count display
  - Empty character name: Skips that player entry

Character Class IDs:
  0 = Amazon, 1 = Sorceress, 2 = Necromancer, 3 = Paladin
  4 = Barbarian, 5 = Druid, 6 = Assassin

functions.name: HandleCreateGameButtonClick
functions.comment:
Handles Create Game button click in Battle.net/LAN multiplayer UI.

Classification: Public API / UI Event Handler

Algorithm:
1. Validate MOTD OK button is active via GetUnitBitMask
2. Get game name from g_pBnetGameNameLabel edit box
3. Convert Unicode game name to Win ANSI (max 255 chars)
4. Validate game name is not empty (strlen check)
5. Get password from g_pBnetPasswordLabel edit box
6. Get difficulty from g_pBnetDifficultyLabel edit box
7. Check if Battle.net mode via Ordinal_10002 (D2Multi.IsBnetMode)
8. If Battle.net mode:
   a. Get max players from g_pBnetMaxPlayersLabel
   b. Set uStack_304 = 1 (game creation flag)
   c. Check max players toggle button validity
   d. Parse max players input or use 0xFF default
   e. Parse level restriction input
9. Convert game name, password, difficulty to title case (16, 16, 32 chars)
10. Build game flags: clear bits 12-14, OR in difficulty level shifted by 12
11. Validate title-cased game name is not empty
12. Branch based on game mode:
    LAN Mode (Ordinal_10002 == 0):
    - Read game flags at g_pGameListData+0x1EA
    - Set expansion flag 0x800 if (flags & 4)
    - Set hardcore flag 0x100000 if (flags & 0x20)
    - Build difficulty char: (expansion?3:0) + diffLevel + '1'
    - Copy difficulty string, call vtable callback at +0x34
    - Show creating game message (string ID 0x147B)
    - Run message pump with CheckVtableAndStopMessageLoop
    - Call vtable callback at +0x98
    - If game creation failed, show error (string ID 0x1412)
    
    Battle.net Mode:
    - Save MAX_PLAYER to registry
    - Save DIFF_LEVEL to registry
    - Check toggle button, save LVL_REST (default 0x29A if disabled)
13. Get local IP address
14. Initialize game join with session data
15. For Battle.net: reset error state, show message, run MCP pump
16. On MCP error, shutdown MCP client
17. Reset UI elements and reinitialize MOTD panel if needed

Parameters: None (uses global UI control pointers)

Returns:
  true (1) - Game creation initiated or completed
  false (0) - Validation failed (MOTD not ready, empty game name)

Special Cases:
- Empty game name after conversion returns false immediately
- LAN mode uses different message flow than Battle.net
- Max players defaults to 0xFF if toggle disabled
- Level restriction defaults to 0x29A (666) if toggle disabled

Registry Keys Written (Battle.net only):
- HKCU\Software\Blizzard Entertainment\Diablo II\MAX_PLAYER
- HKCU\Software\Blizzard Entertainment\Diablo II\DIFF_LEVEL
- HKCU\Software\Blizzard Entertainment\Diablo II\LVL_REST

Flag Bits at g_pGameListData+0x1EA:
- 0x04: Expansion mode flag
- 0x20: Hardcore mode flag

Flag Bits at g_pGameListData+0x204:
- 0x0800: Expansion game flag
- 0x100000: Hardcore game flag

- 0x1412: Game creation error message
